issues.failure_scenario: A terminal-first user runs `npx cookwright init --hosts codex` before ever starting Codex. They then read the README's Codex section, which step 3 sends them to, or the /setup add-host line run from Claude Code, and are told to 'restart Codex'. init's own row says 'open or restart'. The user is unsure whether a first launch counts, or whether they must launch, quit and relaunch. The cost is small: the worst case is an extra restart. But this is the inconsistency the round set out to remove, and a user-facing sentence written in this round brought it back.
issues.evidence: README.md:37 says 'After the first write and after every rewrite alike, restart Codex at the work tree's top'. packages/cookwright/skills/setup/SKILL.md:140 says 'restart Codex at the work tree's top'. init's note at packages/cookwright/src/lib/messages.mjs:235 and :237 says 'open or restart'. README.md:13 (step 3) says 'open it after init, or restart it'. So the Codex paragraph that step 3 points to covers the first write but drops the 'open' case, which is the case finding 0 of QA run 2 was about. The impact is small (worst case is one extra restart) but the inconsistency is real.
